researched_by: the council's own Visitor Management Plan 2026, its published asset list, committee papers from 2008 and 2011, and the operators of the sites it still owns
policy_summary:
Aberdeenshire is a flat prohibition with no provision, and it says so in writing. The Aberdeenshire Visitor Management Plan 2026, published on 27 March 2026, states that 'overnight stays within a campervan or motorhome is prohibited within Aberdeenshire Council car parks (i.e. sleeping within the vehicle)', resting on the standard Scottish conditions-of-use clause that 'no person shall use any part of an off-street car park, or any vehicle left in an off-street car park for sleeping, camping or cooking purposes, other than with the authorisation of the Council'. The same plan draws the distinction that matters: 'a campervan or motorhome can be parked unoccupied overnight within an Aberdeenshire Council Car Park'. What is banned is sleeping, not the vehicle.

There is no aire, no designated bay, no permit and no trial anywhere in the county. Nothing on the council's parking pages mentions motorhomes at all - forty-five towns' worth of car park listings with not one reference to a campervan, an overnight stay or a height barrier. The plan also confirms that the council's counter-measure of choice has been withdrawn for lack of money: 'due to Aberdeenshire Council having no available budget ... Aberdeenshire Council Ranger Service are not employing any Seasonal Access Countryside Rangers over the 2025 visitor management season'. So the position for 2026 is a written prohibition, no rangers to observe it, and no legitimate alternative in the council's gift.

The provision that does exist under this authority is entirely invisible from the parking side of the house, and it is substantial. Aberdeenshire Council is a caravan-park LANDLORD. In 2008 it directly ran ten caravan parks - Aden, Ballater, Banff Links, Fraserburgh, Haughton, Peterhead, Portsoy, Rosehearty, Stonehaven and Turriff - under a single set of council management rules capping stays at three weeks. In 2011 it transferred management of eleven caravan parks to community groups and private operators, and it has been a landlord rather than an operator ever since. Four caravan assets remain on its 1 October 2025 asset list: Ballater, Banff Links and the Haughton Country Park site, all marked 'Leased Out', plus Greenbanks in Banff, which is not.

On access rights the plan is as blunt as the Cairngorms guidance: 'the use of campervan and motorhomes are not covered by the Scottish Outdoor Access Code (SOAC) as it is a motorised activity and the code is only applicable to non-motorised activities', and 'staying in a motorhome or campervan overnight outside a formal site without the permission of the landowner or land manager is not wild camping'.
notes:
THE STEP-2 FINDING IS THE WHOLE FILE. Read the parking pages and Aberdeenshire looks like a council with no relationship to motorhomes at all. Read the asset list and the 2008 area-committee papers and it is one of the largest municipal caravan-site estates in the dataset, disposed of in a single 2011 decision and now let out. Nothing links the two: the parking section does not mention the caravan parks, and the caravan parks do not mention the council.

THE DEESIDE CORRECTION. data/sites/cairngorms-national-park.json records that 'Aberdeenshire Council provides no equivalent anywhere in its part of the park' and that 'Aberdeenshire runs no aire scheme on Deeside'. On aires that is correct and now doubly confirmed - the Visitor Management Plan prohibits overnight sleeping in every council car park, Deeside included, and no bay or permit exists at Ballater or Braemar. But it is incomplete as a statement about council provision. BALLATER CARAVAN PARK IS AN ABERDEENSHIRE COUNCIL ASSET, inside the national park, on Deeside, four miles from Balmoral: sixty pitches on Anderson Road, held by the council and let on a long lease to Ballater Community Enterprise Ltd since 28 February 2012. So the Deeside side of the Cairngorms does have local-authority-owned overnight provision - it is a caravan park under community management, not an aire, and it does not appear on any parking page. The Balmoral/Crathie GBP10 overnight ticket being estate-run is unchanged by anything found here: Crathie is Balmoral Estate land and nothing suggests otherwise.

THE 2011 DISPOSAL, AND WHAT EACH SITE BECAME. Turriff Caravan Park is the clearest account, from the community company that took it: 'in 2011 the council transferred management of eleven caravan parks to community groups or private entities', and Turriff and District Ltd with the community council took theirs over in March 2012. Stonehaven went furthest - the Queen Elizabeth site was community-asset-transferred to Stonehaven Town Partnership at GBP1,000 a year against a GBP12,000 commercial valuation and sublet to the Caravan Club from the 2013 season, with the committee papers noting frankly that 'the static stances on offer at Stonehaven would be very much reduced'. It is now the 79-pitch Stonehaven Queen Elizabeth Park Club Campsite and no longer a council asset. Aden went to Buchan Development Initiative Ltd. Ballater went to Ballater Community Enterprise. Haughton and Banff Links went to commercial operators on long leases.

BANFF LINKS IS COMMON GOOD LAND, and the lease terms are public because the leasehold business was marketed in May 2022 at offers over GBP150,000: a 25-year lease with 17 years unexpired, GBP20,339 a year to the council, 101 pitches split 42 static and 59 touring, open eleven months of the year. That is a council collecting twenty thousand pounds a year in ground rent from a coastal caravan park while prohibiting overnight sleeping in the car park a mile away.

COASTAL PRESSURE IS DOCUMENTED AND UNANSWERED. The Visitor Management Plan's hot-spot tables name Stonehaven beach and harbour for 'irresponsible motorhome/campervan parking, toileting' and Sandend for 'irresponsible camping, tents and campervans, toileting, litter', with Catterline, Crawton, Crovie, Pennan, Portsoy, Gardenstown, Cruden Bay and Port Erroll, Newburgh beach, New Aberdour, Millshore and Cullykhan also listed, alongside Aden, Balmedie and Haddo country parks - and the response offered is a leaflet. Kincardine and Mearns councillors did look at designated overnight campervan spaces in Stonehaven at Mineralwell Park, Baird Park, Backies, the golf course lay-by, the leisure centre, the Co-op car park and Market Square, with the report author recording 'a willingness to look at what provisions might be considered to enable safe informal parking for motorhomes when the caravan site was full', and emergency services raising no objection. Six years later the plan says prohibited. That is the direction of travel: the idea was examined and dropped.

PRIVATE AND COMMUNITY SUPPLY, so nobody re-researches it. Caravan and Motorhome Club sites at Stonehaven Queen Elizabeth Park, Silverbank in Banchory and Huntly Castle. Community or private caravan parks at Turriff, Aden, Rosehearty, Portsoy, Fraserburgh and Peterhead, all former council sites. Port Erroll Harbour at Cruden Bay is run by Port Erroll Harbour Cruden Bay Trust Ltd, which took GBP16,197.84 of the council's Coastal Communities Challenge Fund to refurbish toilets and improve water access for 'harbour users and motorhome visitors' - the closest thing to council-funded motorhome facilities in the county, and it is a grant to a trust, not a council site.
open_questions: What is Greenbanks Caravan Site, Bridge Road, Banff? It is on the council's own asset list as a caravan site that is NOT leased out, which makes it the only one the council may still hold directly. Residential, gypsy/traveller, storage or touring is unresolved.

Is the overnight sleeping prohibition enforced, and how? The Visitor Management Plan states the rule but names no penalty, and the 2019 Off-Street Parking Order PDF is a scan with no machine-readable text, so the excess charge and the schedule of car parks it applies to were not read.

Does the council own the coastal caravan parks at Rosehearty, Portsoy, Fraserburgh and Peterhead in 2026, or were those four sold outright rather than leased? They were council-run in 2008 and are absent from the 2025 asset list, which suggests disposal, but no transfer document was found.

Do any of the council's harbours - Portsoy, Gardenstown, Macduff, Banff, Rosehearty, Johnshaven, Gourdon, Stonehaven - permit overnight vehicle stays or sell waste disposal? aberdeenshireharbours.co.uk could not be read.
Ballater Caravan Park and Banff Links nightly prices for 2026 were not published on any page read.
Aden's pitch detail conflicts: the country park's own page says 21 touring pitches all with electric hook-up plus 10 camping, ukcampsite says 31 pitches with no hook-ups at all.

sites.name: All Aberdeenshire Council car parks
sites.notes: County-wide and unambiguous. The Visitor Management Plan 2026 states 'overnight stays within a campervan or motorhome is prohibited within Aberdeenshire Council car parks (i.e. sleeping within the vehicle)', on the authority of the conditions of use: 'no person shall use any part of an off-street car park, or any vehicle left in an off-street car park for sleeping, camping or cooking purposes, other than with the authorisation of the Council'. Written against any vehicle, not just motor caravans, and it bites on the act of sleeping rather than on the parking - the same plan confirms an unoccupied campervan may be left overnight. No car park anywhere in the county is excepted, and there is no permit or authorisation route published. The instrument is the 2019 Off-Street Parking Order; its scanned text was not readable, so the penalty is unconfirmed and no seasonal rangers are employed to observe it.

sites.name: Ballater Caravan Park, Anderson Road, Ballater
sites.search_hint: Ballater Caravan Park, Anderson Road, Ballater AB35 5QW
sites.notes: OWNED BY ABERDEENSHIRE COUNCIL, inside the Cairngorms National Park on Royal Deeside, and marked 'Leased Out' on the council's 1 October 2025 asset list. Operated by Ballater Community Enterprise Ltd, a subsidiary of Ballater Royal Deeside Ltd set up on 28 February 2012 specifically to run the park on a long lease from the council, with profits going back into the site or the community. Sixty pitches for caravans, motorhomes and tents between the River Dee and the golf course, five minutes' walk from the village. This is the record that qualifies the Cairngorms file's line about Aberdeenshire providing nothing on Deeside: no aire, but a council-owned caravan park under community management. Takes grey water; no chemical disposal advertised.

sites.notes: OWNED BY ABERDEENSHIRE COUNCIL AS COMMON GOOD FUND LAND and leased out. The terms are on record because the leasehold business was marketed in May 2022 at offers over GBP150,000: a 25-year lease with 17 years unexpired from July 2022, GBP20,339 a year to the council paid quarterly, assignation subject to council approval. 101 caravan stances in total, 42 static and 59 touring, plus tents, right behind Inverboyndie beach on National Cycle Route 1. The touring figure is used as the bay count here. Sources differ on the touring split - the sale brochure says 59 touring of 101, caravansitefinder says 58 touring of which 38 have hook-ups.

10 fully serviced pitches with water and grey waste
sites.search_hint: Haughton Holiday Park, Montgarrie Road, Alford AB33 8NA
sites.notes: INSIDE A COUNCIL-OWNED COUNTRY PARK, and the clearest example in this file of provision that the parking pages cannot see. Aberdeenshire Council owns Haughton Country Park outright; the caravan park within it is on the asset list as 'Leased Out' and trades as Haughton Holiday Park. The council's own country park page mentions it only in passing, noting that the Mansion House 'houses self-catering flats and the reception, shop and games room of the caravan park situated within the park'. 129 pitches in total of which 79 are touring or tent - 59 hardstanding with hook-up, 10 fully serviced, 10 grass with hook-up, 30 grass without - the remaining 80 being private holiday-home stances. Open eleven months, which is unusually long this far north.

sites.name: Aden Caravan and Camping, Aden Country Park, Mintlaw
sites.search_hint: Aden Caravan and Camping, Station Road, Mintlaw AB42 5FQ
sites.notes: At the entrance to Aden Country Park, which Aberdeenshire Council owns, and managed and run by Buchan Development Initiative Ltd - a former council caravan park handed to a community body in the 2011 transfer. 21 touring pitches and 10 camping pitches plus glamping pods and one accessible static. Hook-ups are disputed: the country park's own page says all 21 touring pitches have electric, ukcampsite says the site has none. The council's Visitor Management Plan separately lists Aden Country Park as a visitor pressure hot spot with no visitor management staff, which is worth knowing before arriving at a summer weekend.

sites.name: Greenbanks Caravan Site, Bridge Road, Banff
sites.search_hint: Greenbanks Caravan Site, Bridge Road, Banff AB45 1HE
sites.notes: Recorded because it exists on the council's own books and nowhere else. The 1 October 2025 asset list carries 'Greenbanks Caravan Site, Bridge Road, Banff, AB45 1HE' as a council-held recreational property in the Banff and Buchan area, and unlike Ballater, Banff Links and Haughton it is NOT marked as leased out - which would make it the only caravan site the council may still hold directly. It appears in no campsite directory, no tourism listing and no booking system, so it is very likely residential, storage or gypsy/traveller provision rather than touring. Do not plan a night here on the strength of this record; it is a lead, not a site.
